text: Two keys carry this episode, one naming the thing and one saying its kind.
The instance repeats almost nothing. Everything it leaves out is already in the schema it names.
That plain key is an alias for the node identifier, so instance keys stay usable as variable names.
A processor reads this same file, follows the context, and writes the addresses out in full. Nothing is converted.
One property, described from two sides in the same file.
Neither file mentions the other. One writes down an address, and the other answers to it.
Two identifiers here, because one of them has to survive a move. The version is not one of them.
Three keywords did all of this, and the rest was already in the schema. Next time, the same graph, from Python.
